text:
camille: Heads-up — seeing a big render spike on /dash/metrics after today's canary. p95 paint jumped to ~2.2s, flame link shows main-thread time around axis/legend layout. https://perf.internal/abcd 

raj: on it — can you paste a repro route + query? is this only sparklines or larger charts too?

camille: Repro steps: Data -> Range=90d -> group=serviceX -> open the metrics chart. URL: /dash/metrics?range=90&group=svcX. Happens on both canary and prod but way worse on canary.

ben: possibly related to my axis wrapping change in PR #1489 — added extra layout logic for long service names. Could be a sync layout loop. I'll look.

olga: fwiw I saw a client bundle bump in the same deploy (1.2MB -> 1.9MB) due to chunking tweak. That explains parse+eval time increase, but the flame shows layout thrash too.

deploy-bot: canary deploy v2.53.7 rolled to 3 hosts (staging ok).

sarah: try disabling prefix prefetch for charts on canary? suspect prefetch + layout interplay (prefetch might be flooding main thread).

camille: disabled prefetch on one canary host — p95 dropped to ~1.1s immediately. So prefetch seems involved. @marco can you check cache/write path and routing/quotas?

marco: looked at requests — prefetch route 'chart-prefetch' started carrying large payloads. We used to send compact ids; now payload has full label arrays. Default TTL is 60s. If clients parse long label lists on main thread, that'll spike layout.

raj: can you paste the client diff that switched payload shape?

ben: here: ```ts
// old
sendPrefetch({ ids: visibleIds })
// new (accidental)
sendPrefetch({ labels: visibleLabels })
```

olga: ugh, labels include emojis + markdown, often 100+ chars. Serializing and deserializing that on the main thread explains parse/layout pain. Also increases bundle eval if we inline anything.

camille: hotfix ideas: revert PR 1489 (axis change) or keep axis but change prefetch to send ids only. I'd prefer a smaller blast radius — don't revert axis unless necessary.

ben: agree — I'll push a tiny patch to map labels -> ids before prefetch and add a simple check to cap payload size. Opening PR now.

sarah: :thumbsup: also add telemetry for prefetch payload size (histogram) so we can alert if it regresses.

marco: I'll temporarily raise 'chart-prefetch' routing/quota so the canary doesn't get throttled while we validate; will revert after.

camille: plan: ben opens PR, olga watches client parse/paint telemetry, marco bumps quota, raj runs canary smoke. If prod impact observed, ping @oncall.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: v2.53.8 -> canary in 5m.

ben: PR up -> #1496. Quick transform applied: sendPrefetch(ids) + payload-size cap.

camille: update after 12m on canary: p95 ~900ms, parse time returned to baseline. No errors in console.

camille: will keep canary running for 30m then merge to main if stable. Thanks all.
